title: Lunceford's labels and New York as the recording center
summary: Most recordings were made in New York for Decca and Columbia; the industry later moved to Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Did he usually record in New York?
Most of our recordings were done in
New York. I remember one date we did in California, but most of the recordings that I did with him were in New York. Yes.
During the time you were working, he was with Decca and Columbia, wasn't he?
He was with both, yeah. He was --
(Inaudible) it was just with those two labels during the time you were with him.
During the time I was with him. I don't know. Vocalion was an off branch of what, of Decca or what?
I'd have to go look it up. I forget.

I don't know. But I know some of his things were on Vocalion, but as I recall, we recorded mostly for Decca and Columbia back there at that time, and what about Cap, the Cap Brothers, did they have Decca or what? I know we did some things for them. Yeah, we did quite a few things for them.
But we recorded in New York; most all the time our recordings were --
There was an awful lot of recording activity in New York. Most of the bands --
Well, most all of it was in --
(Inaudible) also all of the picket say, when Billie Holiday was going to make a record, she'd call her Friday groups. I mean, (inaudible) and just about everybody.
Yeah. Well, that was because most of the musicians were centered around New York at that time, but you take today. A lot of the musicians are centered out here in Los
Angeles, and so an awful lot of recording going on in Los Angeles.
I think there's (inaudible) probably more here now.

I think so now, but at that particular time almost all of the -- the industry, like the TV -- wasn't too much TV back then. This was before TV. But most all of the radio work and all of your shows like that came out of New York, but I noticed a lot of those shows moved out here after the TV got started, you know. I guess the climate is inducive to things of that sort too, because you don't lose as many days from bad weather and things of this sort.

But New York was really the center of the -- hub of everything in the entertainment field back in that day, you know. And Lunceford's band was a very popular band. At that time when Lunceford was (inaudible) -- there wasn't too many bands doing a lot of recordings that were selling a lot. There were good bands around, very good bands around, because Basie was around at that time, and Basie in -- later on he started really recording things that were really big hits.
